desc:
Clear eBay seller reports show what you sold, what eBay and shipping cost and what you actually kept. Ecom Swift LLC turns your own account data into a plain report on sales, fees, returns and top items, ending with a short list of next steps.

## What is an eBay seller report?

An eBay seller report is a summary of your selling activity in one place: revenue, fees, shipping costs, returns, payouts and the performance of individual items. eBay offers many raw reports and downloads, but they are spread across several screens and rarely answer the question every seller has: how much did I really make?

Our report pulls the figures together and explains them in sentences. It uses only the data in your own account, so nothing is guessed from outside.

## Why raw numbers do not tell you enough

A sales total can look healthy while profit is poor. Selling fees, ad fees, postage, refunds and the cost of the goods all come out of that total. Without a view that puts them side by side, it is easy to keep selling items that earn little and to ignore items that earn well.

Reports also reveal slow changes. A rising return rate, a drop in conversion or a slide in seller level builds quietly across weeks. Spotting it early gives you time to act while the fix is still small.

## How a report improves decisions

A good report lets you decide with evidence. You see which items bring profit, which ones tie up stock and which listings earn views but few sales. You can compare ad fees with ad sales and decide whether promotion is worth continuing.

Returns data points to causes. If one item keeps coming back for the same reason, the fix may be a better description, better packing or a different supplier. We cannot promise how results will move, but a report makes the next choice better informed.

## What a useful eBay report includes

- Revenue, eBay fees, ad fees and shipping costs shown separately.
- Net result after those costs, and after your cost of goods if you share it.
- Best and slowest items by sales and by profit.
- Return numbers and the reasons buyers give.
- Seller level figures and any defects behind them.
- Listing views and conversion, where your account provides them.
- Ad fees set against the sales those ads produced.
- Month-to-month comparison for trend reading.
- A short sentence on what each section means and one action to try.

## What we do

We collect your sales, payout, fee and return data from your account and tidy it into one dataset. We check that totals match between sources, then build the report in plain language, one section at a time, each ending with what it means.

The Basic package covers one month with three suggested actions. The Standard package compares two months and adds a seller level check, ad detail and both a PDF and a spreadsheet. The Premium package covers three months of trends, an item-level profit view, a reusable dashboard sheet and a review call, so you can keep updating it yourself.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Share your cost of goods so profit figures are true.
- Pick a regular day each month to read the report.
- Compare the same period each time.
- Act on one or two findings before looking for more.
- Keep the spreadsheet so you can add new months yourself.

**Avoid:**
- Judging a month on revenue alone.
- Ignoring returns because the sales look strong.
- Comparing a holiday month with a quiet one without adjusting.
- Changing many things at once, which hides what worked.
- Treating one bad month as a trend.

## Who this is for

This service suits a seller who sees money arriving but cannot say what is profitable. It suits a business owner who must explain eBay results to a partner or an accountant, and a seller whose seller level changed and who wants to understand why.

## What we need from you

Tell us which months to cover and share your cost of goods if you can. Let us know any one-off events, such as a sale or a stock loss, that explain unusual figures. We never ask for your password. We read the data through the access eBay allows for your account, or from exports you send us.
